AWS Trade Data Pipeline — Project Guide

Project scope: this project supported BCA (Bank Central Asia), Indonesia.
The data-engineering pipeline starts from structured CINV (Commercial Invoice) CSV batches provided through the client data-transfer workflow.
Upstream systems may extract business documents or export structured files.
From that point, the pipeline standardizes heterogeneous schemas, validates data quality, removes duplicates, reviews unit-price anomalies, creates traceable outputs, and prepares trusted data for AWS analytics.
INQ and PO are related trade-document types, while CINV is the main analytical example.

Four-part learning path: AWS Core, Local ETL, Data Ingestion, and Data Exploitation — with project visuals and interview reinforcement embedded in each part.

☁️ AWS Core — Data Engineer Knowledge Map

Learn the platform first. Four exam-weighted AWS data domains plus a practical IaC track. Open only the module you need; P5 moves from beginner concepts to production Terraform / CloudFormation.

🎛️Orchestration & MessagingStep Functions · MWAA/Airflow · EventBridge · SQS · SNS · Retry · DLQ›07

Step Functions / MWAA orchestrate workflow sequence. EventBridge routes events. SQS buffers work and decouples producers/consumers. SNS fans out notifications.

📨
SQS — decouple a data pipelineKeep the useful flow from the reference: producer → queue → consumer, plus retry and DLQ.
⚙️ProducerIngestion job / Lambda / application
→
📨SQS QueueBuffers messages; consumers pull independently
→
🧰ConsumerGlue trigger / worker / processing service
→
☠️DLQIsolates messages that exceed retry policy
Data Engineer mental model: SQS is not your data lake. It buffers work and decouples producers from consumers. Design around visibility timeout, retry count, idempotency, and a dead-letter queue.
Real data-pipeline use case HIGH

A producer lands orders_2026-10-02.csv in S3 and sends a small message containing bucket, key and run ID. Workers pull messages and start validation independently.

Simulate: 10,000 files arrive at 09:00. SQS absorbs the spike; 20 workers drain the queue at their own rate. Failed files retry and finally move to a DLQ.
Parameters that actually matter

Visibility TimeoutRetentionLong PollingDLQRedrive Policy

Interview trap: standard queues are at-least-once, so consumers must be idempotent. FIFO is only needed when ordering/deduplication requirements justify it.

Real Data Engineer simulation: Package the SFTP downloader with its Python dependencies into a Docker image, push a versioned tag to ECR, reference it from an ECS task definition, and let Step Functions start a Fargate task. The task reads Secrets Manager, downloads the CSV batch, writes S3, emits logs, and exits.
Lower-priority reference extraction: ALB/NLB and EKS are useful architecture literacy, but they are secondary for this Data Engineer learning path. Know ALB as Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS routing, NLB as Layer 4 TCP/UDP/TLS high-performance routing, and EKS as managed Kubernetes. Go deeper only when the target role explicitly owns platform or Kubernetes infrastructure.
📦

Why not EKS here? This workload does not need Kubernetes orchestration. Fargate gives the project a simpler serverless container execution path with less platform overhead.
ECR → ECS/Fargate production path HIGH

ECR stores immutable/versioned container images; ECS orchestrates tasks; Fargate supplies serverless compute. Keep these responsibilities separate.

docker build -t sftp-downloader:1.0 . docker tag sftp-downloader:1.0 ACCOUNT.dkr.ecr.REGION.amazonaws.com/sftp-downloader:1.0 docker push ACCOUNT.dkr.ecr.REGION.amazonaws.com/sftp-downloader:1.0
Simulated ingestion run

EventBridge → Step Functions → ECS RunTask. The task assumes an IAM role, reads SFTP credentials from Secrets Manager, downloads files, writes raw objects to S3, emits logs to CloudWatch, then exits.

Failure: container exits code 1. Keep logs/run ID, retry only transient failures, and never bake passwords into the image.

🧭 ARCHITECTURE MENTAL MODEL

End-to-End AWS Design Flow

Learn the responsibility of each layer first, then map each responsibility to the AWS service that implements it.

⏰ Schedule→🎛️ Orchestrate→📥 Ingest→ ⚙️ Transform→🗄️ Store & Catalog→🔎 Query→📊 Present
⏰01
SCHEDULE
EventBridge Scheduler

Starts the workflow at a defined time or interval.

🎛️02
ORCHESTRATE
AWS Step Functions

Controls workflow order, dependencies, retries, and failure paths.

📦03
INGEST
ECS + AWS Fargate

Runs the downloader container and writes source data into S3 Raw.

🧠04
TRANSFORM
AWS Glue

Reads raw data, applies ETL logic, and prepares processed datasets.

🗄️05
STORE & CATALOG
S3 + Glue Data Catalog

S3 stores processed Parquet data; Glue Data Catalog stores schema and partition metadata.

🔎06
QUERY
Amazon Athena

Uses catalog metadata to query the required processed data in S3.

📊07
PRESENT
Tableau

Sends SQL through Athena and presents returned results as dashboards and visualisations.

🎯 PROJECT FLOW
EventBridge→Step Functions→Fargate→ S3 Raw→Glue→S3 Processed + Catalog→ Athena→Tableau

🛢️RDS & AuroraOLTP · Multi-AZ · Read Replica · Backup · Failover›06

Multi-AZ primarily improves availability/failover. Read Replicas primarily scale reads. Aurora provides a cloud-native distributed storage architecture with MySQL/PostgreSQL compatibility.

🛢️
RDS — OLTP, Multi-AZ and Read ReplicaSeparate availability from read scaling; this is the part most useful to a Data Engineer.
🖥️ApplicationSQL connections
→
🛢️RDS PrimaryTransactional reads + writes
⇢
🛡️Multi-AZ StandbySynchronous standby for failover
📖 Read Replica

Asynchronous copy used mainly to scale read traffic. It is not the same thing as Multi-AZ failover.

💾 Backups

Automated backups and point-in-time recovery protect the database; design retention around RPO/RTO.

Partition keyChoose a high-cardinality key that spreads traffic; poor key choice can create hot partitions.
Sort keyUse it to model one-to-many or time-ordered access inside one partition key.
Capacity modeOn-demand fits unpredictable traffic; provisioned capacity fits predictable workloads when you want explicit capacity control.
Real Data Engineer simulation: For user event state, use PK = user_id and SK = event_timestamp when the access pattern is “read one user’s recent events.” For large analytical history, export or stream data to S3 instead of scanning DynamoDB as a warehouse.

🔑Encryption & SecretsAt Rest · In Transit · KMS · SSE-S3 · SSE-KMS · TLS · Secrets Manager›02
Protect stored data, secrets, and network traffic as separate security concerns.
🔐
Secrets Manager + KMS — secure a Data Engineer workloadCredentials and encryption keys solve different problems. The workload needs both IAM permission and the correct key/resource permissions.
⚙️Glue / ECS RoleTemporary workload identity
→
🔐Secrets ManagerSFTP / DB credential secret
→
🔑AWS KMSProtects encryption keys
→
🪣S3 / RDSEncrypted data at rest
Secrets Manager HIGH

Store passwords, API keys, SSH private keys and database credentials outside code. Retrieve them at runtime with the workload IAM role. Rotation is useful for supported secrets and should be tested with consumers.

Your SFTP example: ECS Fargate starts → assumes task role → GetSecretValue → connects to SFTP → downloads CSV → secret never appears in source code or Docker image.
KMS for a data lake HIGH

KMS manages cryptographic keys; services such as S3, RDS and Secrets Manager integrate with it. With SSE-KMS, access can require both permission to the S3 object and permission to use the KMS key.

Failure simulation: Athena can see the table but query returns AccessDenied on encrypted objects. Check S3/Lake Formation access and KMS key permissions.
Envelope-encryption mental model

Application/service requests encryption → KMS protects the data key → ciphertext is stored with the data → authorized decrypt operations recover plaintext. KMS does not become your bulk data store.

SSE-S3SSE-KMSKey policyIAM policyRotationAudit

Security checklist

Use workload roles, least privilege, encryption at rest and TLS in transit. Keep secrets out of Git, images and logs. Monitor secret/key API activity with CloudTrail and operational failures with CloudWatch.

🧩 Architecture Lab — Private NetworkingNAT Gateway vs VPC Endpoint · private subnet traffic paths · secure AWS service access ›06
🌐

Private Networking — NAT Gateway vs VPC Endpoint

Use these two diagrams to explain where traffic goes from a private Fargate task.

Line : Download via NAT; then upload to S3 through the VPC Endpoint.

1. Secure external SFTP path

The private Fargate task initiates HTTPS through NAT Gateway and Internet Gateway. The response returns through the same path and lands back on Fargate.

2. Private upload to S3 Raw

After Fargate receives the file, it streams or multipart-uploads it to S3 Raw through the S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint. This path does not use NAT or the external network.

DownloadFargate → NAT Gateway → Internet Gateway → Client SFTP Endpoint → back to Fargate
UploadFargate → S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint → S3 Raw
LineNAT = internet; VPC Endpoint = private AWS service access

🧩 Components in this module

What is Infrastructure as Code?

Infrastructure as Code means defining cloud infrastructure in version-controlled files instead of creating resources manually in the AWS Console.

Key point: Code describes the desired infrastructure; the IaC engine creates or changes AWS resources to match it.

Why use IaC?

IaC makes infrastructure repeatable, reviewable, auditable and easier to reproduce across development, test and production environments.

Interview: The main benefit is not automation alone; it is consistent and controlled infrastructure change.

☁️ AWS
ConceptBeginner explanation
DeclarativeDescribe what the final infrastructure should look like, rather than scripting every console click.
Desired stateThe configuration represents the infrastructure you want.
IdempotencyRunning the same configuration again should not create duplicate resources when nothing changed.
DriftThe real AWS environment no longer matches the infrastructure definition because of manual or external changes.

Console changeTag Environment: dev → test
Next planTerraform detects a difference and proposes reconciliation.! Drift
Think of state as Terraform's map: configuration address ↔ real AWS resource identity.
Terraform Code
↔
📘 State
↔
☁️ Real AWS Resources

State is Terraform's mapping between configuration and real infrastructure. It records resource identities and attributes so Terraform can calculate what must change.

Local vs remote state

Local state is acceptable for learning. Teams normally use a remote backend so state is shared, protected and controlled.

Locking and concurrency

Production workflows should prevent two engineers or pipelines from modifying the same state at the same time.

Import

Import brings an existing resource under Terraform management; configuration still needs to describe the resource correctly.

Sensitive state

State can contain sensitive values. Restrict access, encrypt the backend and avoid treating the state file as ordinary source code.

Production rule: Do not commit terraform.tfstate to Git.

🧩Terraform Modules & EnvironmentsModule · input / output · for_each · count · dev / staging / prod · reusable platform patterns›04
🧪 Hands-on Lab 04 — Reuse one module for dev and prod
Project structure
infra/
├── modules/
│   └── s3-data-lake/
│       ├── main.tf
│       ├── variables.tf
│       └── outputs.tf
└── environments/
    ├── dev/
    └── prod/
Root module usage
module "data_lake" {
  source      = "../../modules/s3-data-lake"
  environment = "dev"
  raw_bucket  = "trade-dev-raw"
}
The module contains the reusable design; each environment supplies values.

A module is a reusable package of Terraform resources. Instead of repeating VPC, S3, IAM and ECS definitions for every environment, create a tested module and pass environment-specific inputs.

Root configurationdev / staging / prod
→
VPC modulesubnets · routes · endpoints
+
Data platform moduleS3 · Glue · IAM
+
Compute moduleECR · ECS Fargate

for_each vs count

Use for_each when instances have stable semantic keys; count is convenient for simple indexed repetition.

Environment strategy

Keep environment values separate while reusing the same modules. Production should not be a manually edited copy of development.

Quick decision: Terraform is strong when you want a consistent IaC workflow, reusable modules and infrastructure beyond AWS. CloudFormation is strong when the environment is AWS-only and the team prefers an AWS-native stack lifecycle.

DimensionTerraformCloudFormation
LanguageHCLYAML or JSON
ScopeMulti-provider and multi-cloudAWS-native
State modelExplicit Terraform state and backendAWS manages stack state
Previewterraform planChange Sets
ReuseModulesNested stacks, modules and reusable templates
RollbackHandled through workflow and corrective configurationBuilt-in stack rollback behavior
Typical strengthPlatform standardization and reusable cross-provider IaCDeep AWS-native lifecycle integration

Interview: Why Terraform?

I would choose Terraform when the organization wants a consistent infrastructure workflow, reusable modules and the flexibility to manage infrastructure beyond AWS.

Interview: Why CloudFormation?

I would choose CloudFormation when the environment is AWS-only and the team values a fully AWS-native stack lifecycle and service integration.

30-second interview answer: I use Infrastructure as Code so AWS environments are reproducible and reviewable. For Terraform, I separate reusable modules from environment configuration, keep state in a protected remote backend, review terraform plan in CI/CD, require approval before production apply, and avoid manual drift. 🧩2. Trade Document CSV ETL

Tab 1 ContentsEnd-to-End MapSTAR StoryCore Rules, Code & Outputs

Trade Document Types

CINV is the main analytical document type in this project. INQ and PO are related trade-document types that can follow the same downstream standardization pattern.

TypeMeaningBusiness purpose
CINVCommercial InvoiceRecords an actual sale of goods or services, including seller, buyer, invoice number, date, quantity, unit price, tax, and total amount.
INQInquiry / RFQ-type documentSent before purchase to ask a supplier for price or availability; item and quantity may exist while price is still blank or zero.
POPurchase OrderA formal buyer order after the purchase decision, normally containing supplier, items, quantities, agreed prices, and delivery terms.
 
INQ / RFQ  →  Quotation  →  PO  →  Delivery  →  CINV  →  Payment

One-line story

I built a reproducible and auditable Python ETL pipeline that converts multiple trade invoice CSV files into validated, deduplicated, transformed and traceable output datasets.

AI is my assistant. I use AI to speed up my work, but AI often generates solutions that are more complex than necessary. I review, validate, and simplify the output so it meets the actual requirements without over-engineering or unnecessary code.

Remember:CSV Sources → Quality → Business Rules → Trade Identifier → Outputs → Reconciliation

⭐STAR StoryPART 2 OF 3›02
S

Situation — Why was the pipeline needed?

Start with the business background, not the code.

Business context

The data platform needed to turn structured CINV outputs from upstream document extraction or client CSV exports into trusted datasets for downstream credit, risk and analytics users.

The required period was January 2020 to December 2022.

Data challenge

The input was a batch of multiple structured CSV files, and different client/export versions could omit optional columns such as unit_price.

The solution had to preserve raw client files, normalize schema differences, and avoid manual file-by-file processing.

Situation memory: Multiple CSV files + schema variation + strict business rules + auditable outputs.
T

Task — What did I need to deliver?

Turn the assignment into four engineering objectives.

01Preserve & Combine

Keep CSV files unchanged and union schemas into one staging dataset.

02Validate & Clean

Standardise fields, recompute invoice, deduplicate and identify review cases.

03Transform & Protect

Create the prescribed identifier and generate its SHA-256 representation.

04Explain & Reconcile

Produce profiles, failure reasons, row counts, tests and a run manifest.

Senior-level framing

The task was not only to clean a CSV. It was to create a repeatable data product with clear modules, deterministic rules, separate exception paths, and reconciliation evidence.

A

Action — How did I implement it?

This is the longest part of the answer. Follow the six numbered steps.

1

Ingest, preserve and profile

The pipeline opens the ZIP programmatically, discovers contributing CSV files and filters the required date range.

It performs a schema union: columns missing from older files are added as null so all records share one master schema.

Profiling records null counts, null percentages, data types, distinct counts and key categorical distributions.

2

Validate and standardise

Rules cover month, buyer_name, product category, item description, storey range, reference_no, street, floor area, invoice year and invoice amount.

Invalid records are removed from the accepted flow and written to Failed with an explicit failure reason.

3

Recompute unit price

I use a derived unit-price rule, the invoice commencement year and a configurable assessment_end_date.

The configurable date makes results reproducible instead of changing every time the pipeline runs.

invoice_end = invoice_year + amount ÷ quantityremaining = floor(invoice_end − assessment_end_date) → years + months
4

Resolve duplicate invoice lines deterministically

The composite key uses all original business columns except amount.

For the same key, I retain the highest price and send lower-amount records to Failed as DUPLICATE_LOWER_PRICE.

Same composite key?→Sort price descending→Rank 1: keepRank >1: Failed
5

Flag unusual unit prices with IQR

First, I calculate analysis_unit_price = amount / quantity so flats of different sizes are comparable.

I compare similar flats within the same year, buyer_name, and product category.

Q125th percentile
IQRQ3 − Q1
LowerQ1 − 1.5 × IQR
UpperQ3 + 1.5 × IQR

IQR measures the spread of the middle 50 percent of the analysis_unit_price values.

Values outside the 1.5-times-IQR bounds are flagged for Review, but not automatically rejected.

A flagged record remains in Cleaned and is also copied to Review, because unusual does not automatically mean invalid.

6

Create the identifier and hash

After quality rules, the pipeline builds the required identifier: T + reference suffix + peer amount code + month + buyer initial.

SBBBAAMMT
S fixed prefix
BBB first three reference_no digits, left-padded
AA first two digits of grouped average price
MM transaction month
T first buyer_name character

The clear identifier is written to Transformed, while Hashed contains its irreversible SHA-256 value encoded from UTF-8.

Because the prescribed identifier uses shortened grouped attributes, it is not guaranteed to be a transaction-level unique key.

🧩Core Rules, Code & OutputsPART 3 OF 3›03

Core rules — the five points most likely to be questioned

RuleImplementationWhy
Schema differencesUnion all source columns; missing historical fields become null.Preserves every source attribute without manual edits.
Unit price recomputederived unit-price rule + configurable assessment_end_date; round down to years and months.Reproducible and aligned with the requirement.
DuplicatesComposite business key excludes amount; highest amount survives.Deterministic and auditable duplicate resolution.
Unit-price anomalyUnit price, grouped by year + buyer + product category, using 1.5×IQR bounds.Creates comparable invoice-item peer groups while keeping review cases in the cleaned dataset.
IdentifierT + reference suffix + peer amount code + month + buyer initial, then SHA-256.Follows the prescribed transformation and irreversible hashing requirement.

I organised the implementation as a small Python package rather than placing every rule in one notebook or script.

Presentation-ready STAR answer

Situation: for the BCA Indonesia client workflow, the AWS Trade Data Pipeline needed a programmatic and reproducible way to prepare multiple structured CINV CSV batches for downstream business-activity and risk analytics.

Task: I had to preserve raw data, enforce data quality and business rules, create the prescribed identifier and produce auditable outputs.

Action: I separated the pipeline into ingestion, data quality, transformation, output and orchestration modules. I unioned changing schemas, profiled and validated data, recomputed unit price as amount divided by quantity, kept the higher amount for duplicate business keys, and applied peer-group IQR to unit price for review cases. Finally, I generated the trade identifier and SHA-256 hash.

Result: The pipeline produces Raw, Staging, Profiling, Cleaned, Failed, Review, Transformed and Hashed outputs, together with a run manifest, reconciliation counts and automated tests.

30-second memory:Preserve → Profile → Validate → Invoice → Deduplicate → Review → Identify → Hash → Reconcile.

Review the Local ETL project by responsibility: business context, source boundary, trade documents, canonical transformation, and anomaly review.
🏦BCA Indonesia / CINV Context🔊
What it isA trade-data ETL project that converts structured Commercial Invoice data into a standardized and trusted analytical dataset.
When to useExplain the client, business purpose, and the data-engineering responsibility before discussing implementation.
Key pointBCA Indonesia → trusted CINV data → downstream business-activity and risk analytics.
InterviewWhat was this CINV project for?
The client was BCA, Bank Central Asia in Indonesia. The pipeline converted structured Commercial Invoice data into a standardized and trusted dataset for downstream business-activity and risk analytics. CINV was an analytical input rather than a standalone credit-scoring model.
Note: Lead with the client, business purpose, and your data-engineering responsibility.
📄Structured CSV Source🔊
What it isStructured CINV CSV batches delivered through the client data-transfer workflow.
When to useDefine the upstream/downstream ownership boundary and where this pipeline begins.
Key pointUpstream business workflow → CSV batches → my pipeline.
InterviewWhere did the CINV data come from?
The pipeline started from structured CINV CSV batches delivered through the client data-transfer workflow. Some structured files could come from source-system exports, while document extraction was an upstream responsibility. My responsibility started from the CSV data rather than OCR or PDF parsing.
Note: Keep your ownership boundary clear and do not claim the upstream extraction layer as your work.
🧾INQ / PO / CINV Business Documents🔊
What it isInquiry, Purchase Order, and Commercial Invoice represent different stages of the trade workflow.
When to useExplain the business meaning of the source data before discussing ETL rules.
Key pointINQ asks; PO orders; CINV records the actual sale.
InterviewWhat do CINV, INQ, and PO mean?
CINV means Commercial Invoice and records an actual sale with buyer, seller, quantity, unit price, tax, and amount. INQ means Inquiry or RFQ-type document and is used before purchase to request price or availability. PO means Purchase Order and is the buyer's formal order to the supplier.
Note: Use the business sequence: INQ → quotation → PO → delivery → CINV.
🧠AWS Glue / PySpark + Spark SQL🔊
What it isThe transformation layer that normalizes heterogeneous CSV schemas into one canonical CINV model.
When to useNormalize columns, align schemas, cast types, union DataFrames, and then apply business rules.
Key pointPySpark aligns structure; Spark SQL applies validation, deduplication, derived fields, and anomaly rules.
InterviewHow do heterogeneous CSV files become one canonical CINV dataset?
AWS Glue uses PySpark to normalize column names, add missing columns, cast data types, align schemas, and union the source DataFrames. The result is one canonical CINV model with consistent columns and data types. Spark SQL then applies validation, deduplication, derived fields, and anomaly rules before writing processed data.
Note: This is one of the strongest questions for proving hands-on data-engineering depth.
📊IQR Anomaly Review🔊
What it isAn explainable statistical review rule for unusual unit prices.
When to useFlag potential unit-price outliers for review without automatically treating them as invalid.
Key pointIQR is robust to extreme values; the 1.5×IQR Tukey rule is used as a review heuristic.
InterviewWhy did you choose IQR for unit-price anomalies?
I chose IQR, or Interquartile Range, because it is simple, explainable, and robust to extreme values. The 1.5-times-IQR threshold is the standard Tukey rule for flagging potential outliers. An outlier is routed to Review rather than automatically treated as invalid data.
Note: Describe this as a review heuristic, not as automatic fraud detection.

🔐Network, Large Files & SecurityPART 2 OF 3›02
🔐

Network, Large Files & Security

PART 2 OF 3

These three design considerations explain how the ingestion path stays private where possible, handles large CSV batchs, and remains production-oriented.

🌐

Network

SFTP credentials / SSH key are stored in AWS Secrets Manager and retrieved by the Fargate task at runtime; they are not hard-coded in the container image.

Fargate stays in a private subnet with no public IP. SFTP/SSH access to Client SFTP Endpoint goes through the NAT Gateway.

S3 traffic uses the S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint, so AWS storage access stays on a private path.

📦

Large CSV batches

The downloader streams the source and uses multipart upload instead of loading the whole file into memory.

SHA-256 metadata provides an integrity fingerprint for traceability and duplicate checks.

🛡️

Security & operations

Step Functions starts Glue only after the download and S3 upload succeed; failures can be retried cleanly.

CloudWatch provides logs and operational visibility, while IAM and encryption protect access to the data.

🧩 Components in this module
Use these component cards to review the production ingestion architecture before the interview questions.
📥SFTP / Client Endpoint🔊
What it isSecure batch file-transfer entry point for client CSV files.
When to useReceive structured files from an external client system.
Key pointUse SFTP for controlled batch exchange; keep the client source boundary clear.
InterviewWhat is SFTP, and why is it used here?
SFTP stands for SSH File Transfer Protocol. It acts like a controlled remote file area where the client can place batch CSV files and the downloader can retrieve them. It fits this workload because the integration is batch-oriented file ingestion rather than a real-time transactional API.
Note: Do not describe the client internal database as publicly exposed.
🔐Secrets Manager🔊
What it isManaged storage for SFTP usernames, SSH keys and other connection secrets.
When to useKeep credentials outside Python code and retrieve them at runtime.
Key pointSecrets Manager stores credentials, not the CSV data.
InterviewWhat are SFTP credentials, and why use Secrets Manager?
The downloader needs connection information such as the SFTP host, username, and SSH private key. AWS Secrets Manager stores those sensitive values outside the Python code. The Fargate task retrieves the secret at runtime before connecting to the client endpoint.
Note: Secrets Manager stores credentials; it does not store the CSV files.
📦ECS Fargate🔊
What it isServerless container compute used to run the Python downloader task.
When to useRun short-lived batch containers without managing EC2 worker nodes.
Key pointECS orchestrates the task; Fargate provides the compute.
InterviewHow does the downloader work?
The Python downloader reads the SFTP credentials from Secrets Manager and connects to the client endpoint. It lists available CSV files, identifies new files, downloads them temporarily, and uploads the raw copies to Amazon S3. After the batch completes, the Fargate task exits, so S3 remains the persistent raw storage.
Note: If asked for implementation detail, mention Paramiko for SFTP and boto3 for AWS APIs.
InterviewWhy Fargate instead of Lambda?
The source batches can be relatively large and download duration can be less predictable. Fargate gives more control over runtime, memory, container dependencies, and streaming behavior. Lambda is better suited to shorter and lighter workloads.
Note: Frame this as workload fit; do not claim Lambda simply cannot process large files.
InterviewHow does private Fargate reach the client SFTP endpoint and S3?
The Fargate task runs in a private subnet without a public IP. It reaches the external client SFTP endpoint through a NAT Gateway and Internet Gateway. After download, it uploads to S3 through the S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint so S3 traffic does not need to traverse NAT.
Note: Remember the split: NAT for external egress; VPC Endpoint for private AWS service access.
🗃️Amazon ECR🔊
What it isManaged container-image registry for the downloader image.
When to useStore and version the Docker image referenced by the ECS task definition.
Key pointBuild Python → Docker image → ECR → ECS Fargate.
InterviewHow did you deploy the downloader to production?
I packaged the Python downloader as a Docker image and pushed the image to Amazon ECR. The ECS task definition referenced that image. Step Functions launched the task on ECS Fargate for each ingestion run.
Note: This is the production deployment path for the downloader code.
🔀Step Functions🔊
What it isWorkflow orchestration service for sequencing tasks, retries and failure paths.
When to useCoordinate the downloader and downstream Glue processing.
Key pointUse it for workflow state and retries, not for data processing itself.
InterviewWhy do you need Step Functions?
Step Functions orchestrates the workflow by starting Fargate, waiting for completion, verifying success, and then starting Glue. It also provides retry, catch, status tracking, and an explicit failure path.
Note: The reviewer is checking sequencing, retries, and failure control.
⏱️EventBridge Scheduler🔊
What it isManaged scheduler that starts the ingestion workflow on time.
When to useTrigger the batch workflow on a recurring schedule.
Key pointEventBridge decides when; Step Functions decides what happens next.
InterviewWhy EventBridge → Step Functions → Fargate?
EventBridge Scheduler decides when the ingestion workflow starts. Step Functions coordinates the dependent stages and failure handling. ECS Fargate provides the compute that runs the downloader container.
Note: This is the simplest mental model for the ingestion control flow.
🪣Amazon S3🔊
What it isDurable object storage for raw and processed trade data.
When to useLand immutable raw CSV files and store processed Parquet outputs.
Key pointSeparate raw and processed zones; storage remains durable after Fargate exits.
🧩AWS Glue / PySpark🔊
What it isServerless managed Spark ETL for transformation and standardization.
When to useNormalize schemas, apply business rules and write processed datasets.
Key pointGlue transforms the data; Glue Data Catalog describes the resulting tables.
InterviewHow did you deploy the Glue ETL code?
The ETL logic was implemented as a PySpark script with Spark SQL transformations. The script was stored in Amazon S3 and referenced by the AWS Glue Job. Step Functions started Glue only after the ingestion task completed successfully.
Note: Keep downloader deployment and Glue deployment as two separate code paths.
InterviewWhy use Glue instead of transforming data inside Fargate?
I separate acquisition from transformation. Fargate handles reliable external file ingestion, while Glue is the scalable ETL layer for PySpark and Spark SQL. Glue also integrates naturally with Amazon S3 and the Glue Data Catalog.
Note: The reviewer is testing service boundaries and single responsibility.

🔐Private Access & VPC DesignPART 2 OF 3›02
🔐

Private Access & VPC Design

Three practical controls keep the analytics path private, governed, and easy to explain.

Private Tableau accessAthena Interface EndpointS3 Gateway EndpointClear VPC boundary

Private Access & VPC Design

👤

Private entry

Internal users reach Tableau on EC2 through the approved corporate network or VPN. The EC2 instance stays in a private analytics subnet with no public IP.

🔒

Private Athena API path

Tableau uses the Athena JDBC or ODBC driver. The Athena Interface VPC Endpoint with Private DNS keeps the API call private.

🗂️

Data, metadata & VPC boundary

Athena uses Glue Data Catalog metadata to query processed Parquet in S3, and query-result S3 access can use the S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint.

Separate application and analytics VPCs are a design choice for clearer isolation; a shared VPC with separate subnets is also valid for a smaller environment.

🧩 Components in this module
Use these component cards to review the analytics, access and private-connectivity architecture before the interview questions.
🖥️Amazon EC2 / Tableau🔊
What it isLong-running compute hosting Tableau Server in the analytics subnet.
When to useRun a stateful BI server that needs stable compute and administration.
Key pointTableau controls human access; the EC2 IAM role controls AWS resource access.
InterviewHow do external clients and internal employees access Tableau?
External client users and internal employees are placed in separate Tableau groups. Tableau permissions control which dashboards, data sources, and actions each group can access. The external client can be limited to client-specific views while internal analysts can have broader analytical access.
Note: Human access is controlled in Tableau rather than by giving every user an AWS IAM account.
InterviewWhy is Tableau Server on EC2 while the downloader uses Fargate?
The downloader is a short-lived batch workload, so Fargate is suitable. Tableau Server is long-running and stateful and needs stable compute, persistent storage, and operating-system-level administration, so EC2 is more appropriate.
Note: Compare lifecycle, state, persistence, and administration needs.
🔑IAM Role🔊
What it isAWS workload identity attached to the Tableau EC2 instance.
When to useAllow Tableau Server to call Athena and access required AWS resources without static keys.
Key pointPrefer temporary role credentials and least privilege.
InterviewWhat does the EC2 IAM Role do?
Tableau Server runs on EC2 and uses an attached IAM role as its AWS identity. That role allows the server to query Athena, read Glue Catalog metadata, read processed S3 data, and write Athena query results. End users do not need direct AWS access keys.
Note: This question checks whether you understand application identity versus end-user permissions.
🔎Amazon Athena🔊
What it isServerless SQL query engine over processed data in S3.
When to useLet Tableau submit analytical SQL without operating a warehouse cluster.
Key pointS3 stores; Glue describes; Athena queries; Tableau visualizes.
InterviewWhy does Tableau connect through Athena instead of directly to S3?
S3 is object storage rather than a SQL query engine. Athena provides SQL semantics and Glue Data Catalog provides schema and partition metadata. Tableau uses Athena as the query layer and visualizes the returned result.
Note: This is the clearest one-line responsibility split for the analytics layer.
InterviewWhat is the responsibility split between Fargate, Glue, and Athena?
Fargate runs the short-lived downloader and lands raw files in S3. Glue standardizes and transforms the data with PySpark and Spark SQL. Athena queries the processed dataset for downstream analytics.
Note: Keep this answer short; it is a service-boundary check.
📚Glue Data Catalog🔊
What it isCentral metadata store for databases, tables, columns and partitions.
When to useProvide schema and partition metadata used by Athena.
Key pointThe catalog stores metadata, not the physical trade data.
InterviewWhat is the role of Glue Data Catalog?
The Glue Data Catalog stores database, table, column, data type, S3 location, and partition metadata. The physical CINV data remains in Amazon S3.
Note: Keep storage and metadata conceptually separate.
🪣Amazon S3🔊
What it isObject storage for processed Parquet data and Athena query results.
When to useStore curated datasets and the configured Athena result location.
Key pointPartitioning and Parquet reduce bytes scanned and improve Athena efficiency.
🔌Athena Interface VPC Endpoint🔊
What it isPrivate VPC path to the Athena API.
When to useKeep Tableau-to-Athena API traffic private from the analytics subnet.
Key pointAn interface endpoint is for the Athena API path.
InterviewWhy use an Athena Interface Endpoint and an S3 Gateway Endpoint?
The Athena Interface VPC Endpoint provides Tableau with a private path to the Athena API. The S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint provides private access to S3 data and query-result files. These endpoints reduce the need to route AWS service traffic through a NAT Gateway.
Note: Know the purpose of each endpoint; exact endpoint internals are secondary.
🔒S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint🔊
What it isPrivate VPC route to Amazon S3.
When to useAccess processed data and query-result files without routing through a NAT Gateway.
Key pointGateway endpoints provide private S3 access from the VPC.
📈CloudWatch🔊
What it isAWS monitoring service for logs, metrics and operational visibility.
When to useObserve Tableau/AWS integration and related platform activity.
Key pointMonitoring is separate from authorization and query execution.
